column1: # Shared corpus: what counts as a well-formed line in an operator allow/deny list.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and why it is not a Go table.
# Two pieces of code decide whether an entry is well-formed, and they live in
# packages that cannot import each other (every service here is its own `package
# main`, which is the microservice seam CLAUDE.md asks for):
#   * the GATE      -- parseOperatorList/rejectVersionPin in operatorlist.go, which
#                      refuses to START on a malformed line, and
#   * the CONSOLE   -- validateEntry in console/liststore.go, which refuses to WRITE
# If those two drift apart the failure is not cosmetic and it is not loud: the
# console happily authors a line, commits it, and the next replica to RESTART
# refuses to boot on a policy file the operator was told was fine. The console
# would have bricked the gate through the gate's own safety check.
# So both read this file, and a third assertion checks the one-way property that
# makes the pair safe: CONSOLE ACCEPTS => GATE ACCEPTS. The console is allowed to be
# FORMAT: gate <TAB> console <TAB> ecosystem <TAB> line <TAB> note
#   line:         the literal text, except that a literal tab is written \t
#                 (a tab cannot be carried by a tab-separated file)
# Adding a case here is the cheap way to pin a rule in both services at once.

column5: the ordinary case
hyphens are ordinary
an npm SCOPE is not a version pin -- the leading @ is part of the name
pypi plain name
pypi hyphenated
a Go module path is a name, and its dots and slashes are not separators
case is normalised by malwareKey, not rejected here

column1: # --- versions: a DENY entry may name one release (#155); a name that is not a name is refused

column5: a version-scoped DENY entry (#155): the hijack case, refusing one release and leaving its siblings installable
the same on a SCOPED name: the second @ is the version, the first is the scope
pip's own exact-pin spelling, which is what an operator will copy from a requirements file
a colon is not part of a PyPI name and is not its pin spelling, so this would load and match NOTHING
same on npm: a colon is in no npm name, and the pin spelling is "name@version"

column1: # --- maven: the identity itself carries a colon (#161) -----------------------------

column5: a Maven IDENTITY is group:artifact; the old guard refused every one of these, so a Maven gate could not use these lists at all
two colons name a release: a version-scoped deny
a Maven coordinate without its group names nothing we can match
three colons name nothing in this grammar
an empty version is a typo, not "every version" -- the bare name is how that is written
the same on PyPI

column1: # --- oci is the documented exception: the reference IS the identity (D164) ------

column5: a bare repository
a TAG is well-formed for oci and reduces to the repository -- surprising, so it is pinned
registry-qualified with a tag

column1: # --- whitespace: one name per line, and the gate says so --------------------

column5: a space is how "name version" gets typed by mistake
a literal tab, same mistake with a different key
a line of only whitespace is TRIMMED to empty and skipped by the file parser, so the gate accepts it -- but it is not an entry anyone can add

column1: # --- empty: skipped by the gate's file parser, refused by the console's box ----

column5: an empty LINE is legal in a file (skipped); an empty ENTRY is not a thing to add

column1: # --- comments: legal in a file, never inside an entry the console writes -------

column5: a whole-line comment is legal in the file, but is not an entry
the gate strips the comment and keeps "lodash"; the console must not accept a name with one glued on, because what it would store is not what was typed
